method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, case/recurrence/formula comparison, reverse paraphrase and structural QA. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Examples and exercises for primitive recursive functions: constants, exponentiation, predecessor, factorial, truncated subtraction, distance, extrema, iterated exponentiation, integer division, finite sums and finite products.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Identity is projection, constant n is built by repeated successor after zero, and multiplication with constant 2 gives doubling. Binary exponentiation has base 1 and multiplies by x at each successor; its formal f and g use zero, successor, multiplication and projections.
samples.checks: The constant index 2, projection indices 3,0 and 3,2, and both informal and formal exponentiation recurrences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Predecessor sends zero to zero and y+1 to y; a dummy argument and projection produce the official recursion, then composition removes the dummy. Factorial sends zero to one and multiplies the preceding factorial by y+1; a two-place helper gives the official scheme.
samples.checks: The total natural-number predecessor, dummy-argument construction, constant-one base and multiplication/successor projections are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Truncated subtraction is zero when x<y and otherwise x−y, with recursion by predecessor. Distance is the sum of both directed truncations. Maximum is x+(y dot-minus x), with both cases checked. Minimum is left as an exercise and problem.
samples.checks: Every inequality direction and operand order is preserved; in particular y dot-minus x occurs in the maximum formula and x/y order remains unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Problems ask for primitive recursiveness of a tower containing y copies of 2 and of floor integer division, with division set to zero when y=0 and an explicit recursion/composition definition required.
samples.checks: The tower brace annotation, floor formula, exceptional denominator-zero value and construction requirement are all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Primitive recursive functions are closed under finite sums and products. Finite sums use the base f(x-vector,0) and add f(x-vector,y+1) at the successor step.
samples.checks: Both sigma/product bounds run from 0 through y, and the proof's successor summand uses y+1.

source_observations: MR-P140 directly attests क्रमगुणित, greatest-integer and division terminology; MR-P141 directly attests महत्तम and लघुतम for function values.
MR-P142 attests घातफल for fixed-base exponential functions, while the displayed two-variable recurrence controls the edition's broader घातांक फलन label.
T307 records छाटलेली वजाबाकी as a transparent formula-controlled label; no exact official Marathi headword was found.
T308 records पूर्णांक भागाकार and the finite sum/product compounds under the displayed formulas and explicit y=0 convention.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact compounds छाटलेली वजाबाकी, पूर्णांक भागाकार, सांत बेरीज and सांत गुणाकार remain expert-reviewable.
